title: Comparative assessment of the corneal endothelium following phacoemulsification surgery in patients with type II diabetes and nondiabetes

license.statement: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (article <license>, text statement); not CC BY, record kept private

indication: Grade I-III nuclear sclerosis (LOCS III), age 50-70 years; type 2 diabetes with good glycaemic control (HbA1c below 7) versus non-diabetic patients operated in the same period; phacoemulsification (Oertli CataRhex, 2.8 mm clear corneal incision, HPMC 2%) with in-bag IOL by one surgeon; excluded prior ocular surgery, uveitis, corneal opacities, glaucoma, pseudoexfoliation, grade IV nuclei, glucocorticoid treatment

groups.description: Type 2 diabetes with good glycaemic control, 40 eyes of 40 patients
Non-diabetic control group, 40 eyes of 40 patients

series.baseline_label: Preoperative central ECD by specular microscopy (Topcon SP-1P) of the operated eye
series.notes: Table 2 'Diabetic group' column (header Mean±SD) at preoperative, 4 weeks (28/30.4375 months) and 12 weeks (84/30.4375 months); no per-visit n

series.baseline_label: Preoperative central ECD by specular microscopy (Topcon SP-1P) of the operated eye
series.notes: Table 2 'Nondiabetic control group' column (header Mean±SD) at preoperative, 4 weeks (28/30.4375 months) and 12 weeks (84/30.4375 months); no per-visit n

exclusions.what: sjopt_226_23-t003 R5-R6 mean ECD change from preoperative
exclusions.reason: changes of the same groups; the absolute ECD series is used

exclusions.what: ECD loss percentages in Results text

notes: Diabetic versus non-diabetic groups are patient-condition subgroups receiving the same standard phacoemulsification; both recorded as control with the condition in indication.
Prospective case-control study, March 2018 to January 2019; one eye per patient.
